findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — response.statusText !== "OK"` is the sole success check on the Salesforce token response; `statusText` is not guaranteed to be "OK" (e.g. HTTP/2 responses have no reason phrase and `statusText` is often `""` in undici/fetch), so a legitimate 200 response can be misclassified as a failure (or vice versa via a non-standard client), masking real refresh outcomes.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:9 — redirect_uri was changed from templated `WEBAPP_URL + /api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` to hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`; could not verify in this sparse checkout that `appConfig.slug` in packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/config.json equals "zoho-bigin" (file not present in checkout), so behavioral drift for the Zoho OAuth redirect_uri contract could not be confirmed or ruled out.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:87 — response.statusText !== "OK"` is used as the HTTP-success check for the token refresh call; `statusText` is not guaranteed to be the literal string "OK" across fetch implementations/HTTP versions (e.g. HTTP/2 clients and some polyfills return an empty string even for 200 responses), so this can incorrectly throw on legitimate successful refreshes. Prefer `response.ok`/`response.status`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` don't express "any string key" — `z.string().toString()` just stringifies the Zod schema object into a fixed literal property name, so this schema silently does not do what the comments claim ("any property with a number is the expiry" / "allow other properties"); a future maintainer reading this will reasonably assume it's a generic passthrough when it is not.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — prisma` is used in `prisma.credential.update(...)` but never imported in this file, so every `getClient()` call (run unconditionally in the constructor, not just on token expiry) throws a ReferenceError, breaking all Salesforce calendar operations with no try/catch to recover or report a clear error.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called with no try/catch; a malformed webhook body throws and results in an unhandled 500 with no structured error message for the caller, instead of a clear 400 response.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:22 — If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset/empty (e.g. admin enabled APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED but forgot to set the secret) and the caller omits the secret header entirely, `req.headers[headerName]` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` are both `undefined`, so `undefined !== undefined` is false and the check passes, letting an unauthenticated caller write OAuth credentials for any userId

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6 — The computed zod schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string keys "ZodString" (or similar) and "ZodOptional<ZodString>", not a dynamic/catch-all key pattern as apparently intended, meaning `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not actually validate "any numeric property is an expiry" as the comment claims — a single unit test feeding a realistic token response (e.g. `{access_token, expires_in, token_type}`) would fail against this schema in the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED path and immediately expose the bug, but no such test exists

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single literal string key (e.g., `"ZodString"` / similar), not a catch-all/dynamic key pattern. So the schema will require that specific property name rather than accepting arbitrary numeric expiry fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date`. In the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` path, `safeParse` will therefore fail on realistic token responses and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`, breaking refresh flows (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom now call this function).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4 — refreshOAuthTokens` branches into 3 distinct behaviors (sync endpoint call when sharing enabled + endpoint set + userId present; otherwise fallback to `refreshFunction()`) and does not check `response.ok`/status before returning the sync-path response, yet none of the branches (sync success, sync HTTP failure, and the two fallback conditions where userId is null or config is unset) are covered by any test

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and immediately `return response;` without checking `response.ok`/status. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap in error handling for the new branching behavior. The claim about “none of the branches … covered by any test” can’t be conclusively verified from this diff alone (no tests are added/updated here, but existing coverage isn’t visible), so the test-coverage portion is at most an important process concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:74 — New refresh-on-connect logic added to `conn`/connection setup performs a live-style OAuth refresh fetch, checks success via `response.statusText !== "OK"` (fragile — statusText is a non-normalized string that can differ by runtime/proxy, e.g. "" on some fetch polyfills, unlike checking `response.ok`/status code), parses the response, and writes to `prisma.credential.update`, but there is no test exercising refresh success, refresh HTTP failure, or invalid-token-shape rejection paths

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new refresh-on-connect fetch checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`. `statusText` is not a reliable/normalized success indicator across runtimes/polyfills (and can be empty or differ from "OK" even on 2xx responses), so this can incorrectly throw on successful refreshes; `response.ok`/`response.status` would be the correct check. The finding’s note about missing tests is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff, while the fragile `statusText` check is directly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:1 — hubspot, googlecalendar, larkcalendar, office365calendar, office365video, and webex CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter files were all modified to route token refresh through the new shared `refreshOAuthTokens`/`parseRefreshTokenResponse` pipeline, but since none of these integrations have any existing unit tests, there is no verification that the new wrapping preserves prior refresh behavior (e.g. correct token merging, refresh_token retention) across any of the 6 integrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new shared refresh helpers (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) and updates several integrations (e.g., Hubspot `lib/CalendarService.ts`, Google/Office365 calendar services, Office365 video, Webex) to call them instead of their prior direct refresh logic. These helpers introduce nontrivial conditional behavior (switching to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, relaxing token schema via `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, and even forcing a `refresh_token` value when missing). The PR does not add any tests in the diff to validate that each integration’s refresh flow still matches prior behavior (e.g., refresh_token retention/merging). The finding’s claim that there are *no existing* unit tests in the repo for these integrations can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the “no new verification for changed behavior” concern is diff-grounded.
